newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan unions threaten Nov 15 general strike.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan unions threaten Nov 15 general strike.

text.p: Venezuela's powerful National Public Sector Workers Union (Fedeunep), which embraces 700,000 state employees, has threatened a general strike for Nov. 15 unless the government honored promised salary bonuses, Fedeunep said.
"If we don't get what they've agreed to give us, we'll go on an indefinite strike," Fedeunep Secretary General Carlos Borges told reporters.

Borges said overdue payments totalled 100 billion bolivars ($213 million). But government officials, who have already placed a spending request with congress, say the amount is only 68 million ($145 million).

Borges met with other union leaders and Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar to discuss a range of requests, including a doubling of the current minimum monthly wage to 100,000 bolivars ($213) on January 1.
"We're asking that the bonuses (agreed in April) become a permanent part of the salary," Borges said.

Annual inflation, currently running at over one hundred percent, has eaten into real wages. According to Central Bank figures, Venezuelan wages had already dropped 53 percent in real terms between 1988 and 1995.
